item.title: India calls for WTO compliant measures to address trade distortions, dumping & predatory pricing
item.dc:creator: News On AIR
item.description: India has called for a WTO-compliant approach to correcting global trade distortions on the concluding day of the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwaukee, US. Speaking on structural excess capacity and production, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said India shares the concerns of many Members that trade-distorting support in some economies can lead to […]
item.content:encoded:
India has called for a WTO-compliant approach to correcting global trade distortions on the concluding day of the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwaukee, US.  Speaking on structural excess capacity and production, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said India shares the concerns of many Members that trade-distorting support in some economies can lead to dumping and predatory pricing.
 
He said such concerns are addressed through WTO-consistent measures, including anti-dumping and countervailing duties, based on evidence and subject to judicial review. He emphasised that industrial capacity in itself is not the issue, while distortions can arise where geographical concentration of production is driven by hidden subsidies and support. He said diversification of production and supply chains is a legitimate objective but cannot be used as a pretext for measures outside WTO rules or for shifting the burden of adjustment onto developing countries, which must retain policy space to industrialise.
 
He also said that sharing of statistics and data should take place within existing mechanisms. Mr Goyal said that India is the fastest-growing large economy in the world, with a domestic-demand-driven economy serving 1.4 billion people. He highlighted that India is building manufacturing value chains from design to finished goods as a trusted link in global supply chains. He said India’s manufacturing capacity serves its domestic and global needs and India does not have structural excess capacity in the sectors identified by the G20 Presidency.
 
An Akashvani correspondent reported that Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said India’s trade with G20 members depends on a transparent, non-discriminatory, rules-based trading system. He said Most-Favoured-Nation treatment is a key guarantee of this system, ensuring that the same terms apply to the smallest trader and the largest trader. Speaking on ending forced labour in global supply chains, Mr Goyal said India’s commitment to the elimination of forced labour is absolute and unconditional.
 
The Minister reaffirmed India’s commitment to a rules-based, fair, equitable, non-discriminatory, transparent, open, inclusive and multilateral trading system with the WTO at its core. He emphasised the importance of preserving policy space for developing countries to grow and feed their people, while upholding decision-making by consensus. On the sidelines, Mr Goyal held bilateral meetings with his counterparts from Australia, Saudi Arabia, and South Korea, among others.

item.title: G7 countries agree to release 100 million barrels of diesel & crude oil as prices climb record high in US
item.dc:creator: News On AIR
item.description: The Group of Seven (G7) nations have agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil over four months in an effort to ease soaring fuel prices, with a substantial release of diesel planned in the first 20 days. The decision came as diesel prices in the United States climbed to record levels, adding pressure on […]
item.content:encoded:
The Group of Seven (G7) nations have agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil over four months in an effort to ease soaring fuel prices, with a substantial release of diesel planned in the first 20 days. The decision came as diesel prices in the United States climbed to record levels, adding pressure on President Donald Trump and his administration ahead of November’s midterm elections. Mr Trump said that European countries had agreed to release large quantities of diesel from their stocks and that the process would begin “immediately.”

The announcement followed an overnight conversation between Trump and French President Emmanuel Macron. According to a statement issued by France after the meeting, the International Energy Agency (IEA) will coordinate the release. The G7 and partner countries will make a coordinated release of 100 million barrels over four months, with a substantial amount of diesel to be released during the first 20 days.

The move comes as fuel prices have surged in the United States and other countries amid the eight-month-long war involving Iran. US diesel prices have risen sharply in recent weeks. The national average stood at 6.37 dollar per gallon on Friday, according to AAA, after reaching a record 6.52 dollar per gallon on September 22.

item.content:encoded:
The United Nations has welcomed India’s approval of the 1.86 lakh crore rupee Green Energy Corridor Phase-III (GEC-III), describing the grid strengthening and battery storage scheme as a major step that will deliver “big dividends” for the country’s people and economy. In a statement to a news agency, UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell said the initiative would help India harness its growing renewable energy capacity, meet rising electricity needs and further strengthen its position as a global leader in solar energy.

He said the scheme would help integrate renewable energy into India’s power system while supporting economic growth. Stiell also highlighted the strategic importance of battery storage for large economies such as India, particularly in the context of energy security and economic growth.

The UN official further said that stronger electricity grids and battery storage infrastructure could generate employment across manufacturing, construction and energy storage as the global transition towards renewable energy and clean technologies accelerates. The Union Cabinet has approved GEC-III with a total outlay of one lakh eighty-six thousand four hundred five crore rupees, including fifty-four thousand eighty-two crore rupees in Central Financial Assistance, to strengthen intra-State transmission systems and support deployment of Battery Energy Storage Systems.
